newsitem.title: USA: NYC says gets $550 mln of large institution orders.
newsitem.headline: NYC says gets $550 mln of large institution orders.

text.p: New York City got about $550 million of so-called "priority orders" placed by large institutions, which helped it cut yields on nine maturities from 2.5 basis points to 10 basis points for its tax-exempt bonds, a city official said Wednesday.
"Priority is what drives pricing," said the city official, who declined to be named.
The maturities in the $834 million issue of general obligation bonds whose yields were cut ran from the year 2000 to 2002, and 2007 to 2012.
But there was a bit less demand for some term bonds, which mature in 2016 and 2024, so their yields were increased by two basis points, the city official said.

He said that the city's tax-exempt offering was almost entirely sold, as adding the $550 million of priority orders to the $270 million of retail orders placed during the presale period produces a total of $820 million.

The $434 million refunding portion of the offering saved the city "a little over $30 million," for its current 1997 fiscal budget, the official said. On a present value basis, the city estimated it saved about $26 million or more than six percent, a level considered unusually rich.
